questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Australia as I was curious about cultural life as well as exploring nature. In addition, Australia has top ranking universities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Most information was relatively easy to obtain.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: At the University of Queensland, there is a pretty extensive orientation week, which focuses on social wellbeing as well as academic support.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I chose a college on campus called International House. This one has the most exchange students from around the world. However, there are multiple colleges at the University of Queensland.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I chose a fully catered option, so I went to the dining hall for all meals (but could also sign up for packed lunches/dinners if I was not home). However, you can also choose a non-catered version with your own kitchen in a apartment with 4 people.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
The average age is around 20 years. 
I found it nice that I did not have to share a kitchen with anyone because it seemed like a huge issue for people living in apartments off campus.
I liked living close to the university, but it was a bit more difficult getting to the center of Brisbane city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There are some pretty helpful tools available to see which courses clash etc. You can check the enrolment criteria as well as other course information in a so-called "course profile" online. Even when the semester has started, it is possible to change your courses for some time.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: E.g. the tool "UQ Planner" where you can insert courses and design your own schedule.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Somewhat successful. However, I experienced that even as a master student in Denmark, I was still only allowed to take undergraduate courses. Some exceptions can perhaps be made if you contact the professors of the course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you meet the enrolment criteria for courses or have some backup courses in mind in case you are not eligible for your first priorities. On the university's website, you can also use a filter that only shows courses that are eligible for exchange students.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some of my courses were at a challenging level, while most of them were fairly easy to keep up with.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I experienced that I was not reading as much as I do at my home university. Instead, I had to engage more actively in classes and prepare something for each week. Exams are different as assessment activities are distributed throughout the semester, e.g. one assignment is 30% of your grade etc.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
PSYC2040 Social and Organisational Psychology 
MGTS2603 Leading and Managing People
SOCY3329 Qualitative Social Research

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
MGTS2603 Leading and Managing People

I found that all students in this class enjoyed attending class. It was always very engaging and active. However, you have to want to participate in group work.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not unexpected, but you have to apply for OSHC as an overseas exchange student and of course you also have to pay for a student visa.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: You can get a 50% discount on public transport in Brisbane as a student.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As an exchange student, I can really recommend QUEST. They arrange a bunch of excursions, parties etc. for exchange students.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of clubs you can even imagine. In the beginning of the semester, you can check them all out in the great court.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Explore the nature and beaches in Queensland.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Gold Coast, Stradbroke island, Moreton island - these can be explored on a day trip.

I also went to New Zealand, Sydney, K'gari/Fraser island and Cairns. Lastly, I went to Uluru in the northern territory, which I can strongly recommend as this was a very special place.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy. Australians are mostly open and also really helpful.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness to meet other people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Join QUEST.
2. Remember to keep up with school work during the semester and not just at the end.
3. There is a broad selection of courses, so choose something that you find interesting even though it might differ somewhat from your field of study.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can follow UQ clubs etc. on social media. Oftentimes, there will be different events at campus (e.g. puppy cuddling, painting etc.)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to meet other exchange students from around the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Coordinating group work that had to be completed every week (only goes for some courses)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
